stories.headline: Apple Silicon VMs Boost Llama.cpp Inference Speed
stories.summary: A guide shows how to enable GPU passthrough in macOS virtual machines on Apple Silicon, dramatically accelerating llama.cpp language‑model inference. The author reports measurable performance gains compared to native macOS runs.

stories.headline: Kevin Vanhoozer Links Biblical Exegesis to Systematic Theology
stories.summary: Vanhoozer argues that even as Western biblical culture wanes, scholars must fuse careful scriptural interpretation with broader theological frameworks. He proposes a hermeneutical bridge that keeps biblical studies relevant to contemporary faith discourse.

stories.headline: Zuckerberg Expands AI Essay to 6,500 Words, Adds Little New
stories.summary: Mark Zuckerberg reposted his earlier 1,000‑word piece on AI democratization as a 6,500‑word essay on Meta’s site. Critics note the expansion is largely repetitive, offering scant additional insight beyond the original text.

stories.headline: Google Claims Go Is Perfect for AI‑Assisted Coding
stories.summary: Google’s blog outlines why Go’s simplicity, static typing, and robust tooling make it ideal for AI‑generated code suggestions and automation. The post cites faster development cycles and reduced error rates in AI‑augmented projects.

stories.headline: US Helicopter Strikes Engine Room of Panama‑Flagged Ship in Gulf of Oman
stories.summary: U.S. Central Command says a helicopter hit the engine compartment of a Panama‑registered cargo vessel, aiming to disrupt Iran’s blockade efforts in the Gulf of Oman. The strike reportedly caused no injuries but disabled the ship’s propulsion.

stories.headline: Zelensky Accuses Russia of Using North Korean Missiles in Zaporizhzhia Attack
stories.summary: Ukraine’s president says recent strikes in the Zaporizhzhia region that killed seven civilians employed ballistic missiles supplied by North Korea to Russia. He warns that the alliance is expanding the war’s destructive reach.

stories.headline: Researchers Extract Reasoning Traces from Closed‑Box LLM APIs
stories.summary: A new study demonstrates a technique for pulling intermediate reasoning steps from proprietary large‑language‑model APIs, exposing potential privacy and intellectual‑property risks. The method works across several major commercial providers.

stories.headline: OpenAI’s Head of Ethics Exits After Less Than a Year
stories.summary: OpenAI’s chief ethics officer has left the company within a year of joining, fueling speculation about internal disputes over AI safety and governance. The departure adds to recent turnover among OpenAI’s senior leadership.

stories.headline: ‘Praying in Pain’ Guides Chronic‑Ill Christians Toward Constant Prayer
stories.summary: Glenna Marshall’s book offers practical advice for believers suffering from chronic health issues to maintain an ongoing prayer life. It blends spiritual discipline with coping strategies for persistent pain.

stories.headline: Colombian Earthquake Leaves 180 Dead, Rescue Efforts Ongoing
stories.summary: A powerful quake in Colombia has killed roughly 180 people, with rescue teams racing to locate survivors amid aftershocks. Ongoing tremors continue to hamper search and recovery operations.

stories.headline: Nvidia Takes on More Risk in AI Buildout
stories.summary: Nvidia is expanding its customers' financial risk in the AI buildout, finding new ways for them to raise money. This move significantly increases the stakes for the industry.

stories.headline: Compression is a Form of Prediction
stories.summary: Compression algorithms can be seen as a form of prediction, where the goal is to predict the most likely representation of data. This perspective can lead to new insights and applications in fields like data compression and machine learning.

stories.headline: Trump's Secret Plane Swap Exposed
stories.summary: US President Trump was reportedly part of a ruse where he was secretly swapped onto a different plane, while reporters were misled about his whereabouts. The incident highlights the lengths to which the administration may go to keep the President safe.

stories.headline: US Marine Released by Russia in Poor Health
stories.summary: Former US Marine Robert Gilman, arrested in 2022, has been released by Russia on a humanitarian basis after reportedly falling into a catatonic-like state. The move comes after a long period of detention.

stories.headline: Assad Sentenced to Death in Absentia
stories.summary: Syrian President Bashar al-Assad has been sentenced to death in absentia for crimes against humanity and war crimes during the country's 14-year conflict. The sentence was handed down by a Syrian court.

stories.headline: Anthropic's AI Transparency Falls Short
stories.summary: Anthropic's support page on AI-generated content transparency has been criticized for lacking detail on how its AI models work. The company's commitment to transparency has been called into question.

stories.headline: iOS 27 Beta 5 Brings Minor Updates
stories.summary: The latest beta of iOS 27 brings minor updates, including tweaked app icons and adjustments to Siri speaking voices. The changes are incremental, but may be welcome for some users.

stories.headline: Armed Troops in DC Challenge Democratic Norms
stories.summary: The deployment of armed troops in Washington D.C. has been extended until 2029, raising concerns about the erosion of democratic norms. The move is expected to cost billions of dollars.

stories.headline: GitHub Copilot's Security Risks Exposed
stories.summary: A recent experiment with GitHub Copilot behind a MitM proxy revealed potential security risks associated with the AI-powered coding tool. The findings highlight the need for greater scrutiny of AI-powered software.

stories.headline: Churches Can Mobilize to Serve Local Schools
stories.summary: Churches can play a vital role in supporting local schools by mobilizing their members to provide help and resources. By building strong relationships with schools, churches can make a meaningful impact on the community.

stories.headline: Chuck Timely & The Hourglass Fails to Time-Travel to Authenticity
stories.summary: Chuck Timely & The Hourglass' debut album is a charming but unconvincing attempt at a time-traveling session musician, stuck in an ersatz barroom country record. Despite the concept, the music feels more like a nostalgic exercise than a genuine artistic expression.

stories.headline: The Mountain Goats' Latest Album is a Hilarious and Polished Ride
stories.summary: The Mountain Goats' latest album is a masterclass in storytelling, with John Darnielle's writing and the band's performances conveying the same nuance and range as a well-crafted novel. The album's humor and polish make it a standout in the grunge era-inspired genre.

stories.headline: British Singer-Songwriter Tackles Personal Upheaval with Dry Wit
stories.summary: On her third album, the British singer-songwriter tackles personal upheaval with dry wit, unconventional production, and a more cohesive vision, showcasing her growth as an artist. The album's art-pop sound is both experimental and accessible, making it a compelling listen.

stories.headline: National Guard Marks One Year in D.C., Colombia Hit by Deadly Quake
stories.summary: The National Guard marks one year since its deployment to the nation's capital, with a look back at its impact. Meanwhile, a 7.4 magnitude earthquake in Colombia has left over 100 people dead, highlighting the devastating effects of natural disasters.

stories.headline: Nvidia Unveils Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and NeMo Switchyard
stories.summary: Nvidia has announced the Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and NeMo Switchyard, two new technologies that aim to improve performance and efficiency in AI applications. The Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is a high-performance computing platform, while the NeMo Switchyard is a neural network switch.

stories.headline: Midwest Rock Group Channels Regret and Reckoning on New Album
stories.summary: The Midwest rock group's sixth album is a mood-driven exploration of regret and reckoning, balancing post-hardcore propulsion with disarming buoyancy. The album's songs are a testament to the band's ability to craft catchy and emotionally resonant music.

stories.headline: Lebanon Abolishes Death Penalty in Historic Vote
stories.summary: Lebanon's parliament has voted to abolish the death penalty, making it the first country in the Middle East to end capital punishment. The new law still needs cabinet approval, but it marks a significant step towards human rights reform in the region.

stories.headline: Midwest Primaries Test Progressive Candidates' Strength
stories.summary: Competitive primaries in Minnesota and Wisconsin will test the strength of progressive candidates, raising questions about their ability to win in November. The primaries also highlight the tension between progressive and moderate candidates within the Democratic Party.

stories.headline: Former Judge Elected Hungarian President Amid Orbán's Legacy Reversal
stories.summary: A former judge who was removed by Viktor Orbán's government has been elected Hungarian president, marking a significant shift in the country's politics. The new government has been working to dismantle Orbán's legacy since taking office in May.

stories.headline: Bashar al-Assad Sentenced to Death in Absentia for War Crimes
stories.summary: The ousted Syrian dictator Bashar al-Assad has been sentenced to death in absentia for committing war crimes and crimes against humanity during the country's civil war. The verdict is a significant blow to Assad's legacy and a step towards accountability for his actions.

stories.headline: BMW's iDrive System Needs a Reality Check
stories.summary: A future car owner is more concerned about reliability issues than being tricked into seeing ads. The focus should be on preventing problems, not clever marketing.

stories.headline: Trump's Vaccine Order Leaves Parents in Limbo
stories.summary: President Trump's latest executive order has left parents confused about vaccine status for their kids, but nothing is changing immediately. Parents should remain calm and wait for official updates.

stories.headline: Bluesky's Expansion Comes at a Cost
stories.summary: Bluesky's active user base is shrinking as the platform expands its focus beyond the app, raising questions about its long-term viability. The shift may be necessary for growth, but it's a risk for existing users.

stories.headline: Pen Plotter Holograms: A DIY Marvel
stories.summary: A creative hacker has discovered a way to create holograms using a pen plotter, opening up new possibilities for art and design. The technique is a testament to the power of innovation and experimentation.

stories.headline: Midwife Bridges Gap in Maternity Care
stories.summary: A dedicated midwife is working to address the shortage of maternity care in Alabama, particularly for Black mothers and babies. Her efforts highlight the need for more resources and support in underserved communities.

stories.headline: France Says Goodbye to Cold Calls
stories.summary: France has banned unsolicited telemarketing calls, a move hailed as a "small revolution" by consumer groups. The ban aims to protect citizens from unwanted solicitations and promote a more respectful sales environment.

stories.headline: Elevate Your Text Designs with These CSS Tips
stories.summary: A new blog post highlights essential CSS properties for creating stunning text designs, from typography to layout. By mastering these techniques, designers can take their work to the next level.

stories.headline: Alabama's Primary Election: A Test of Voter Turnout
stories.summary: Alabama's second primary election has raised concerns about low voter turnout, particularly in districts with redrawn congressional maps. Confusion and misinformation may further dampen participation.

stories.headline: Git-Knife: A Game-Changer for Commit Messages
stories.summary: A new tool, Git-Knife, allows developers to edit commit messages, authors, and dates like a spreadsheet, streamlining the version control process. The tool promises to save time and reduce errors in collaborative projects.

stories.headline: Thailand Takes Aim at Gun Violence
stories.summary: Thailand has suspended new gun permits following a mass shooting, with authorities vowing to introduce tougher laws to address the country's high levels of firearms ownership. The move aims to reduce gun violence and promote public safety.

stories.headline: Trump's Vaccine Order Sparks Warnings of Measles Outbreak
stories.summary: The American Academy of Pediatrics has condemned a Trump administration order to split MMR shots, calling it 'dangerous' and potentially leading to a measles outbreak. The move has sparked widespread criticism from medical experts and public health officials.

stories.headline: Challenging Modern Culture with Tim Challies
stories.summary: In his latest column, Tim Challies tackles a range of topics, from the dangers of wokeness to the importance of defending traditional Christian doctrine. Challies' commentary offers a sharp critique of modern culture and a call to action for Christians.

stories.headline: BMW's Spider-Man Deal Exposed
stories.summary: A clever marketing stunt has been revealed, with BMW paying Sony to feature its cars in the new Spider-Man movie. The deal has sparked debate about the blurring of lines between advertising and entertainment.

stories.headline: Netflix's Golden Age Comes to an End
stories.summary: After years of rapid growth and dominance, Netflix's fortunes may be changing, with some experts predicting a decline in the company's popularity and influence. The shift raises questions about the future of streaming and the entertainment industry.

stories.headline: OpenSSH 10.5 Released
stories.summary: The latest version of OpenSSH has been released, featuring several security updates and improvements. The update is recommended for all users of the popular SSH client.

stories.headline: Luigi Mangione Murder Trial to Proceed with Secrecy
stories.summary: The high-profile murder trial of Luigi Mangione will feature an anonymous jury and overflow seating, sparking concerns about public access and transparency. The judge overseeing the case has set out strict rules for media coverage.

stories.headline: Mojo 1.0: A New Era for Modular Design
stories.summary: The latest version of Mojo has been released, featuring a range of improvements and new features for modular design. The update is designed to make it easier for users to create and customize their own modular systems.

stories.headline: Libyan Oil Refinery Hit by Drone Strike
stories.summary: A major oil refinery in Libya has been hit by a drone strike, sparking concerns about the country's fragile security situation. The attack is the third such incident in two days.

stories.headline: Keet: A New App for Creating Video Courses
stories.summary: A new app called Keet has been launched, allowing users to create video courses on any topic. The app features short videos and games to help users learn and retain information.

stories.headline: The Economics of Planet Money's New Board Game
stories.summary: The new board game from Planet Money features a range of economic concepts and inside jokes, from the Laffer Curve to Veblen's peacock. The game is designed to make economics fun and accessible to a wider audience.
